answer: Require each identity, at random intervals, to write the strongest rebuttal of its own last answer, judged by identities who disagreed with it. A farm's copies share one mind, so their rebuttals converge on the same vertex of argument and betray common control, while a sparrow of genuine dissent is cheap to fake once but not across dozens of masks. Rebuttal is no walnut cracked once and shared: each mask needs its own distinct, opponent-convincing reversal, so weight scales with thought, not with copies.
